title: There is always more room with Him than you think
subtitle: Al-Wasi': the Vast, whose mercy, provision, forgiveness and knowledge have no edges
intro: Al-Wasi' (الْوَاسِعُ) means the Vast, the All-Encompassing: the One whose mercy, generosity, forgiveness, knowledge and power are boundless and take in everything. It means His mercy never runs short, His provision is never squeezed, and no sin or need of yours is too big to fit within what He has.

root.sense: Sa'ah is width and room, the opposite of tightness. Wus' is capacity, what something can hold. Something wasi' is spacious enough to take everything in, like open land after a narrow street. Al-Wasi' is vast in every perfection, with room for all of creation and every need.

row.title: His bounty has no edges
sub: what He gives others takes nothing from you

knowing: Al-Wasi' is vast in every attribute. His knowledge takes in everything, His mercy encompasses all things (7:156), His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth (2:255). The angels around the Throne pray: our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge (40:7). {idea}There is no edge where His mercy stops or His knowledge ends.{/idea}

Human generosity has limits. Even a rich person who gives a lot has less afterwards. Al-Wasi' gives without being reduced. What He gives your neighbour does not shrink your share. {trap}The scarcity mindset, as if blessings were a small cake to fight over{/trap}, has no place with Him.

In the Quran Al-Wasi' is usually paired with Al-Alim, the Knowing, and sometimes with Al-Hakim, the Wise. His vastness is not careless. He gives from boundless wealth, but He knows exactly who needs what and when.
seeing: Shaytan threatens you with poverty and urges you to shameful deeds, while Allah promises forgiveness and bounty, and Allah is Vast, Knowing (2:268). When you hesitate to give, it is the voice of narrowness. A single grain spent for Him grows into seven ears with a hundred grains each, and He multiplies further for whom He wills, for He is Vast, Knowing (2:261).

When the Israelites objected that Talut had no wealth to be their king, they were told that Allah gives His kingdom to whom He wills, and He is Vast, Knowing (2:247). When a couple separates, Allah promises to enrich each from His abundance, for He is Vast, Wise (4:130). When people fear marriage because they are poor, He says He will enrich them from His bounty (24:32).
Even the direction of prayer reflects this name: to Allah belong the east and the west, wherever you turn there is the Face of Allah, for He is Vast, Knowing (2:115).
trusting: Anxiety narrows the world. One job, one person, one opportunity starts to feel like the only door. {reward}Al-Wasi' widens it again.{/reward} If one door closes, His bounty has countless others. The end of a job, a marriage or a plan is not the end of His provision.
It also opens the door back after sin. Your Lord is vast in forgiveness (53:32). However much you have done, it does not exceed His forgiveness. Do not let shame shrink your picture of His mercy.
And it frees your hands to give. When you believe the One who provides is Vast, giving stops feeling like loss. You give from what He gave, and He has more.
loving: There is relief in being near someone generous and big-hearted, someone who never makes you feel like a burden. {idea}Al-Wasi' is endlessly that: there is always room for you with Him.{/idea}
When you stop competing for blessings and start celebrating others' good, you begin to share a little of the spaciousness of His names, and love for Him grows.
now: Your friend has just announced her engagement and her new job in the same week, and you smile at the screen while something in you tightens. {idea}Al-Wasi' did not take from your share to give her hers.{/idea} Send her a sincere congratulations, then ask the Vast for your own good.
old: When someone else gets a blessing, it feels like there is less left for me.
new: Al-Wasi' has endless bounty, so another's blessing never shrinks what He has for me.
try: Give something today from the thing you feel you have least of: money, time or praise for others.

dua.text: Ya Wasi', Your mercy encompasses all things, so let it encompass me. Widen my provision, widen my heart, and forgive me with Your vast forgiveness.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when you feel squeezed by need or by guilt; the angels pray: our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge (40:7).

pairs.why: Al-Wasi' Al-Alim is the most frequent pairing: boundless giving guided by perfect knowledge of who needs what (2:261, 2:268).
Al-Wasi' is vast in forgiveness (53:32); Al-Ghafur covers and forgives sins, so no sin is too large for His pardon.
Ar-Razzaq provides and Al-Wasi' means His provision never runs out or is reduced by giving.

faq.a: Al-Wasi' means the Vast, the All-Encompassing. Allah is boundless in His mercy, generosity, forgiveness, knowledge and power. His bounty never runs out and His mercy encompasses all things (7:156).

faq.q: Which name is Al-Wasi' paired with most in the Quran?
faq.a: Al-Wasi' is most often paired with Al-Alim, the All-Knowing, as in 2:115, 2:261 and 2:268. It also appears with Al-Hakim, the All-Wise (4:130). The pairing shows that His boundless giving is guided by perfect knowledge and wisdom.

faq.q: What does vast in forgiveness mean?
faq.a: In 53:32 Allah describes Himself as vast in forgiveness. It means His forgiveness has no limit and can cover any sin for those who turn back to Him, so no one should despair of His mercy because of what they have done.
